question: Tertiary blast injuries are caused directly by the pressure wave of the explosion and are the same as primary blast injuries.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. The four blast injury types differ by mechanism: Primary = pressure wave barotrauma; Secondary = fragment/shrapnel penetration; Tertiary = displacement by blast wind causing blunt impact; Quaternary = burns, crush, toxic inhalation. Tertiary and primary are not the same.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Primary blast injuries are caused by the pressure wave (barotrauma — tympanic membrane, lungs, GIT). Tertiary injuries occur when the victim is thrown by the blast wind and strikes a surface, causing blunt trauma. They are entirely distinct mechanisms.
